video_title: Stephen A. says ’THE KNICKS ARE GOING TO THE FINALS!’ 🏆 | First Take

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. believes Knicks will reach finals but winning is tough
quotes.excerpt: But winning it over OKC or Wembanyama and San Antonio, that's a tall, tall order.
quotes.quote: Winning? We gotta pump the brakes. We gotta pump the brakes. OKC and San Antonio just appear to be next level. Is it impossible for the New York Knicks to beat either one of those teams? No. But it's highly unlikely. You almost need pretty much close to perfection from the New York Knicks for them to have a chance to beat either of those teams in the Western Conference. I'm not a Dallas Cowboy fan. I'm not delusional. I make sense. I'm not delusional at all. I'm gonna hold on to the fact that the New York Knicks, what I said at the beginning of the year, they're going to the NBA Finals. I firmly believe that. But winning it over OKC or Wembanyama and San Antonio, that's a tall, tall order. But I reserve the right to address that once the finals are here.

quotes.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Russo believes Knicks are dangerous and will be competitive in finals
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are dangerous. They can score, they can play pretty good defense.
quotes.quote: I think, listen, this is the kind of win that makes you start to believe a little bit. I mean, they've been playing really well. Well, they've been playing really well, but the Knicks had laid an egg and not won the game and Cleveland won and the Knicks lose by 15. It's like, geez, here we go again. But the fact that they got off the deck and won this crazy game miraculously, first game, what, in the history of the NBA, somebody was 22 down in the seven minutes to go. To do that, they're flying at home. They got a lot of belief right now. Listen, they played San Antonio pretty well in the regular season. They won two out of three. And the game they lost, they only lost by two. So maybe I'm not saying they're gonna win the final, but I think they will be more competitive than I thought they would be prior to what we've seen with the Knicks in the last say three, four weeks. Since that Atlanta game three, or game four, when they were down two games to one. The Knicks are dangerous. They can score, they can play pretty good defense. They've played 10 guys last night. Brunson will make a big shot. OG Anunoby didn't do anything and they still won the game. This is a dangerous team. I don't think they win the NBA championship, but I now think that final will be very, very competitive and I wouldn't have said that a long time ago.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst highlights Knicks' special resilience and refusal to quit
quotes.excerpt: This is a team that had quite a ride during this regular season, but you watch how they're coming together.
quotes.quote: This is the fourth time in the Jalen Brunson era that the Knicks have come back from 20 down to win a playoff game. You remember last year those two games? The Celtics. So, this is one of the things you think about a team that's special. Obviously when the Knicks play great and everything goes well, they can win. They're two of 19 on threes through like two and a half quarters of this game. That's a loss, right? But this is, what we're seeing right now in 20 years, people are gonna be remembering this team. Jalen Brunson will be sitting courtside in the seats that Patrick Ewing is in. And people will remember 2026 because of how special this team is. And I think we can agree that this is a special team. This is a team that had quite a ride during this regular season, but you watch how they're coming together. This last month, there's something special going on. They will be the underdogs if they win three more games here, they will be the underdogs, absolutely. But this team is special. And the other thing I liked about it, maybe they wouldn't have come from the down, but nobody in the building left because they've seen the team come back. Nobody on the Knicks ever looked like they quit at all. You could argue that the Cavs quit on the game. It was the Knicks who didn't quit. So, when you ask me, am I more confident? Yeah, I am. I am not gonna be in the business of underestimating this Knicks team.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. describes Jalen Brunson's demoralizing impact on the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson just let them know, 'I'm here, and there's nothing that you all can do about it.'
quotes.quote: This aura, this belief like, yo, it's just that dude right there. That's what Brunson did to Harden and the Cavaliers last night. He just said he just let them know, 'I'm here, and there's nothing that you all can do about it. I'm here, and I'm going to take y'all out.' He took their heart. Now, all of this is null and void if they lose game two. I understand that. I just don't think it's going to happen. I think that was a devastating loss last night by the Cleveland Cavaliers. And I think it's the kind of loss in the postseason you simply do not recover from.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian and Stephen A. debate Cavaliers' ability to bounce back after Brunson's dominance
quotes.excerpt: The manner in which you saw Jalen Brunson giving it to them last night. Did you see that?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Probably. I will just say something about the Cavs. The Cavs are eight and seven in the playoffs. They have had some disappointments. They had a game in Toronto where RJ Barrett bounced around and went in. They bounced back from that. They get down 2-0 to the Pistons. They bounced back from that. They have a chance to win the series last Friday at home, lay an absolute egg. They bounced back from that. So, I agree with you, Stephen A., but I will just say, don't quite say that this one. The Cavs could bounce back tomorrow night.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: Well, Windy, let me ask you this, Windy. We've seen Kevin Durant drop damn near 40 against them. We've seen we saw Paolo Banchero do his thing. He had 38 in the loss or whatever. The manner in which you saw Jalen Brunson giving it to them last night. Did you see that? Did you see that in these playoffs against the Cleveland Cavaliers? You didn't see that. It's one of those things. What I'm trying to say is that it's literally one of those moments where you're James Harden and you're probably home and you question how soon it's gonna be before you retire. Like you just ain't what you used to be. Because James Harden, we've never considered him an elite defender. We don't hold against him his lack of defensive prowess. We're not expecting some elite defender out of him. But we didn't see him get his ass kicked like that. We didn't see him get iso'd like that. We didn't see him get embarrassed like that. That was the kind of ass kicking in that fourth quarter that you see how Donovan Mitchell walked back to that locker room? I don't give a damn what he said on that podium. It's like, yo, what are you talking about? Did you watch what we watched? Jalen Brunson gave it to him. You Harden, you sitting there home like, you know, that's what I used to do to people. Now I know how all those people felt when I spent years doing it to them. Because that's what Brunson did to him.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
text_blocks.text: Winston-Salem State. All right, Steve, take it easy. Winston-Salem, take it easy.
